validity.recommendation: Keep all P5543 values as recorded. Do not merge/confuse with P0767 or P1439 (the separate, later 'Ukhta-Torzhok Stage I/II (Yamal)' system) despite the near-identical Russian names and shared Gazprom project-page URL pattern.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real via multiple documents (Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta's own Urdomskoye LPUMG page and 2017 anniversary newspaper, Gazprom Invest's encyclopedia page, ru.wikipedia's 'Сияние Севера' article, and a 2025 regional-press article on a modernization/dismantling plan for its sibling strings) -- not a GEM-only or hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural-gas trunk/transmission pipeline (fuel=Gas, type=transmission); no evidence of NGL or gathering/feeder misclassification. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other row in this batch -- P5541 (String I, 1969, 1220mm), P5542 (String II, 1975, 1220mm) and P5543 (String III, 1977-78, 1420mm) are three genuinely distinct physical pipe strings built in sequence, confirmed via a single primary source (Urdomskoye LPUMG page) that lists all three with distinct years/diameters in one passage. THE ACTUAL FINDING: this batch's real risk is a SOURCING/DISAMBIGUATION hazard, not a wrong value. Russia's gas-transport network has TWO different 'Ukhta-Torzhok' systems that share nearly identical Russian names and even the same Gazprom-family URL pattern: (1) the OLD Vuktyl-era system built 1969-1978 as three parallel 'nitki' (strings) -- P5541/P5542/P5543, this row's family; and (2) a NEW, much later Yamal-era system built 2012-2017 in two stages, both 1420mm/9.8 MPa/45 bcm/y -- corresponding to GEM rows P0767 and P1439. The CURRENT_REF already on file for P5543's Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Location (proektirovanie.gazprom.ru/.../ukhta-torzhok/) is PRIMARILY a project page about the NEW system's Stage II (i.e. it is actually P1439's correct dedicated primary source, not P5543's). On close reading, that page does contain one passing but explicit and useful sentence naming the OLD trio by number ('Ухта — Торжок (I, II, III нитки)') as existing, currently-operating parallel infrastructure in the same corridor -- so it is not actively WRONG as a supporting reference for this row, and no data value here needs to change. But a future researcher skimming only the page title/topic could easily paste this same URL onto P0767/P1439's Status/Location cells thinking it is redundant, or could mistake P5543's own StartYear/Diameter for the Yamal system's, given both are named 'Ukhta-Torzhok' with Roman-numeral stage/string labels. Verdict is 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than 'concern' because no recorded value on this row is actually wrong -- the caveat is purely a documentation/disambiguation note for whoever next touches P5541, P5542, P0767, or P1439.

Directly supports Status=operating for this specific segment, not just the aggregate corridor.

Komiinform (regional press, independent of Gazprom), 2025-04-10, on a Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta modernization plan: names only 'Ukhta-Torzhok 1' and 'Ukhta-Torzhok 2' for planned dismantling (5.4 MPa lines being replaced by 9.8 MPa lines). String III (1420mm, built 1977-78, a different generation from I/II's 1220mm) is conspicuously NOT named for demolition -- negative/contextual evidence that String III continues operating unaffected as of this most recent dated evidence.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Required status-review verdict for P5543 (operating row). No source found describing String III as shut down, dismantled, mothballed, or under active decommissioning planning. On the contrary, the most recent dated evidence (Apr 2025) is a Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta company announcement of a modernization plan that explicitly targets its OLDER, lower-pressure sibling strings (I and II, both 1220mm/5.4 MPa, commissioned 1969/1975) for dismantling and replacement, while conspicuously not naming String III (1420mm, built to a newer/larger spec in 1977-78) -- consistent with String III continuing in normal operation. VERDICT: CONFIRM operating, no change.
